editorial.approach: Use a two-pointer approach, starting `left` at 0 and `right` at n - 1. Swap elements at `left` and `right`, then increment `left` and decrement `right` until they meet.

hints: You can solve this by swapping elements from both ends of the array.
Use two pointers: `left` initialized at 0, and `right` initialized at `nums.length - 1`.
Loop while `left < right`. Swap `nums[left]` and `nums[right]`, then increment `left` and decrement `right`.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Create a new array, traverse the original array backwards, copy elements into the new array, and then copy them back to the original array.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use the two-pointer approach to swap elements in-place from both ends inward, using O(1) auxiliary space.

interviewExplanation: Reversing an array can be done in O(n) space by allocating an extra array, but in interviews, an in-place swap using two pointers is expected. This achieves the same O(n) time complexity while reducing the space complexity to O(1).
